name: Pedashur
title: Father of Gamaliel, leader of the Manasseh tribe
summary: Pedashur is known from the Book of Numbers as the father of Gamaliel, who was the head and leader of the Manasseh tribe during the wilderness journey. He is mentioned in connection with the census and the organization of the tribes at Sinai. Although little is known about him personally, his family played an important role in Israel's early organization.

keyEvents.title: Appointment of Gamaliel as tribal chief
keyEvents.description: Pedashur's son Gamaliel was appointed leader of the Manasseh tribe when the tribes of Israel were organized in the wilderness.

keyEvents.title: The Census in the Wilderness
keyEvents.description: Gamaliel, son of Pedashur, led the counting of the Manasseh tribe, which numbered 32,200 men fit for battle.

keyEvents.title: Camp Arrangement Around the Tabernacle
keyEvents.description: Gamaliel, son of Pedashur, was assigned a place for the Manasseh tribe on the west side of the tabernacle under the banner of Ephraim.

keyEvents.title: The Offering at the Altar
keyEvents.description: Gamaliel, son of Pedashur, brought his tribal offering at the dedication of the tabernacle's altar on the eighth day.

keyEvents.title: Commander of the army of Manasseh
keyEvents.description: Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur, was placed over the military division of the tribe of Manasseh when the Israelites broke camp from Sinai.
